jobs.title: Staff Program Manager, Organizational Change Management
jobs.description:
Overview

Intuit's CTREC organization (Cybersecurity, Trust & Safety, Risk, Enterprise Systems and Compliance) protects the company and powers the technology experiences of our global workforce. We're looking for a Senior Change Manager to own organizational change management (OCM) delivery and adoption strategy for CTREC's most critical programs — the changes that touch every Intuit employee, from security protocols to enterprise systems to employee-experience technology.

This is a hands-on leadership role, not an advisory one. You will craft the change strategy for each program and personally execute every piece of it — communications across channels, enablement content, stakeholder engagement, and adoption measurement. There is no separate design or communications team behind you, and no runway to learn the discipline on the job. Skilled, self-directed OCM leadership is essential to adoption success from day one.

You'll operate as part of the Change COE — the team that designs the human layer around technology change so employees don't just get access to something new; they understand it, want it, and can use it well. The COE matches its response to the size and risk of each change: it Drives the highest-impact changes end to end, Supports moderate ones by contributing strategy while the owning team executes, and Consults as the fast expert check on lower-risk changes. You'll flex across all three modes and partner with the OCM lead to define the engagement model and tiered level of support for each initiative.

Responsibilities

Own end-to-end OCM delivery and adoption strategy for critical CTREC programs — from impact assessment through launch, adoption, and reinforcement.
Build change strategy from scratch and execute it end to end yourself: audience and impact analysis, adoption plans, success metrics, and risk mitigation — with no reliance on separate design or communications resources.
Develop and deliver communications for multiple channels (email, Slack, intranet, in-tool messaging, executive briefings), right-sized to audience and moment.
Create enablement content — guides, FAQs, training assets, self-service resources — that helps a distributed global workforce understand, embrace, and adopt change.
Drive stakeholder engagement across all levels, from frontline employees to senior leadership, building the coalitions each change needs to land.
Partner closely with Development, the Product lead, and the Technical Program Manager as an embedded member of the program team, and align strategy with the OCM lead.
Flex across the Change COE's engagement tiers — Drive, Support, or Consult — matching depth of involvement to the size and risk of each change, and partner with the OCM lead to define engagement models and tiered levels of support across the portfolio.
Invent creative, low-friction adoption solutions — resourceful ways to reach and activate distributed audiences and build trust in automation that acts on a user's behalf.
Develop and implement change management tools and processes that accelerate change activities, ensure a consistent change experience, and standardize communication approaches across programs.
Monitor employee feedback channels to address questions and gauge sentiment on Security change initiatives, feeding insights back into program decisions.
Measure adoption, gather feedback, and iterate — closing the loop between user sentiment and program decisions.

Qualifications

7+ years of change management experience supporting large, multi-site enterprise implementations of HR, IT service, Security, or employee-experience technology.
Proven ability to own change strategy from scratch and execute it end to end personally — you are the strategist, writer, designer, and facilitator in one.
A track record of creative, low-friction adoption solutions that reached and activated distributed audiences — including building user trust in automation acting on their behalf.
AI platform fluency — you use AI tools and platforms fluently in your own work (research, content development, analysis) and can guide others through AI-driven change.
Excellent writing and content-design skills across formats and channels, with the judgment to right-size comms to the change.
Strong stakeholder management — comfortable partnering with engineering, product, and program leaders and influencing without authority.
Self-direction and speed: you scope ambiguity into a plan, prioritize independently, and deliver without needing the role explained to you.
Strong proficiency applying ADKAR or an equivalent structured change methodology within condensed go-live timelines and high stakeholder expectations.
Proven ability to manage concurrent workloads under a fixed deadline, sequencing communications across phased waves to prevent audience fatigue and message conflicts.
Strong executive communication skills — comfortable drafting on behalf of senior HR and technology leadership for enterprise-wide distribution.
Domain experience across collaboration SaaS applications, HR, and Security, with a working understanding of data security and compliance concepts.
Skilled in impact analysis, stakeholder mapping, and developing communication and care/readiness plans.
Technology company experience implementing change efforts that impact technologist/development organizations as well as business functions.
Project management experience leading cross-functional teams to achieve business goals.

Who You Are

Customer obsessed — inspired by the customer problem, partnering with process owners to drive change, education, and outreach.
A strong process and systems thinker, sees how changes, channels, and audiences interact across a portfolio, and builds repeatable tools, standards, and mechanisms rather than one-off fixes.
Demonstrates extreme ownership, delivers excellence at scale, and operates without boundaries.
Influences and drives decisions by crafting a clear point of view — options, data-backed recommendations, and rationale — and builds a compelling, data-backed case for change.
Proactively identifies obstacles, develops recommendations for resolution, and escalates to leaders quickly.
Quickly establishes credibility and trust across teams; leads with inquiry and incorporates diverse perspectives to deliver high-impact outcomes.
Resilient and solution-oriented in a high-change, often ambiguous environment, with a data-led and data-driven approach focused on long-term opportunity.
Proactive, action-oriented self-starter with high judgment, innovation, and strategic thinking; strong organizational and time-management skills.
Works independently and collaborates effectively across cross-functional teams and with employees at all levels, using inquiry and advocacy to work through barriers.

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

As a Data Analyst, Fraud, you will be part of Remitly's Identity & Trust Analytics Team. You will develop a deep understanding of Remitly's fraud detection systems, regional risk profiles, and operational processes to improve fraud defenses while maintaining a seamless experience for legitimate customers. Develop and track risk metrics that quantify fraud exposure, policy compliance, and system performance.

jobs.description:
Join the Clean Energy Revolution

Become a Program Manager, Business Resiliency & Weather Services (Advisor)
at Southern California Edison (SCE) and build a better tomorrow. In this job, you’ll lead the planning, coordination, and execution of strategic programs and initiatives that support Weather Services, emergency preparedness, wildfire mitigation, and operational resiliency across the enterprise. You will partner with technical experts, operational organizations, and senior leadership to drive cross-functional projects, improve processes, manage program governance, and deliver actionable insights that strengthen SCE's ability to anticipate, prepare for, and respond to operational risks.

As a Program Manager
, your work will help power our planet, reduce carbon emissions and create cleaner air for everyone. Are you ready to take on the challenge to help us build the future?

Responsibilities

Partners with key business units to develop and lead planning and response teams maintain or develop response plans in the event of severe but plausible operational disruptions.
Supports business resiliency incident management activities within the crisis management processes and monitor lessons learned.
Performs gap analysis on assessment findings to identify critical business processes, resources, and key personnel.
Continuously improves and enhances business resiliency plans and recovery strategies. Collects, analyzes, and presents key metrics to senior management.
Researches and identifies relevant requirements and procedures to implement best practices in crisis management and business resiliency.
Supports the development and maintenance of key program documentation including the reporting and supporting material for risk committees and other governance groups.
Monitors critical and important incidents, identifying the cause, remediation, future risks, and escalating to leadership as needed.
A material job duty of all positions within the Company is ensuring the protection of all its physical, financial and cybersecurity assets, and properly accessing and managing private customer data, proprietary information, confidential medical records, and other types of highly sensitive information and data with the highest standards of conduct and integrity.

Minimum Qualifications

Seven or more years of experience in business resiliency, emergency management or utility operations.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Business, Emergency Management, Engineering, Meteorology, Public Administration, Environmental Science, or related field.
Experience with MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
Experience leading complex, cross-functional programs or projects within utility operations, emergency management, wildfire mitigation, meteorology, risk management, or business resiliency.
Demonstrated experience developing executive presentations, briefing materials, governance reports, and strategic communications for leadership audiences.
Experience facilitating collaboration among technical experts, operational organizations, and corporate functions to achieve strategic objectives.
Knowledge of utility emergency management, incident management systems, operational readiness, business continuity, or resiliency frameworks.
Experience developing and monitoring key performance indicators, metrics, dashboards, and program reporting.
Experience with data analytics, business intelligence tools, and Microsoft Office applications including Power BI, SharePoint, Teams, and the Microsoft Power Platform.
Experience with AI technologies and productivity tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot) to improve business processes and operational effectiveness.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills with experience managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Proven ability to influence stakeholders and drive alignment across organizations with competing priorities.
Exceptional organizational skills with high level of initiative and ability to effectively interface, collaborate, and partner with executives, senior management, clients and team members to help drive solutions and ensure stakeholder buy-in.
Demonstrate sound leadership skills to set priorities, achieve desired actions and outcomes through facilitation, collaboration, negotiation and influence.

Additional Information

This position’s work mode is hybrid. The employee will report to an SCE facility for a set number of days with the option to work remotely on the remaining days.  Unless otherwise noted, employees are required to work and reside in the state of California.  Further details of this work mode will be discussed at the interview stage. jobs.description:
Position Purpose:
Design, implement and monitor IT controls for core applications and systems. Analyze IT data to assess risk and improve processes and efficiency.

Key Details:
Conduct various Risk Assessments of information technology systems and internal processes. Recommend controls to mitigate loss of information assets to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of sensitive data while meeting the core organizational mission of Centene.

This is a remote position within the United States. Candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for employment-based visa sponsorship now or in the future. Sponsorship and future sponsorship are not available for this opportunity, including employment-based visa types H-1B, L-1, O-1, H-1B1, F-1, J-1, OPT, or CPT.

Assess security risks of systems, applications, processes with emphasis on cybersecurity risks against common control frameworks and regulations including but not limited to HIPAA, NIST, ISO-27001 and make recommendations to mitigate.
Utilize qualitative and quantitative analysis methods to assess risk and provide outputs to risk stakeholders.
Design, monitor and evaluate controls for effectiveness and efficiency to mitigate areas of risks based on Centene's defined risk appetite.
Prepare finalized reports stating identified risks, and their recommended controls for stakeholders to make treatment decisions. Prepare and document standard procedures and protocols.
Review and prepare scheduled audit reports from both internal and external requests.
Design application and system level controls in adherence to best auditing and security practices.
Interact with business owners to identify key controls and coordinate appropriate measurement efforts for process improvement.
Complete optimization reviews and prepare audit reports associated with the completion of scheduled audits.
Assist with designing the IT environment to conform to relevant industry standards, such as ISO 27001, HIPAA, Sarbanes-Oxley, PCI-DSS and other related state requirements.
Assist with evaluation of controls against security best practices.
Serve as primary liaison between auditing bodies, IT security management, compliance and business stakeholders.
Assist with implementation of department strategy related information systems and technology architecture.
Performs other duties as assigned.
Complies with all policies and standards.

Education/Experience

Bachelor's degree in IT, MIS, Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, related field or equivalent experience.
3+ years of combined auditing and IT controls design experience.
Knowledge of IT systems and processes and experience evaluating internal technical control systems required.

CISSP, CRISC, CISA, CISM, FAIR, CPA, or CIA preferred.

jobs.description:
Description

Your passion belongs at UNC Health. Join more than 56,000 teammates working together to improve the health and well-being of the communities we serve across North Carolina.

Summary

The Business Intelligence Analyst (BIA) provides insight-driven analyses and insights that enhance decision-making. The BIA is an analytics professional who leads reporting and data visualization development in partnership with stakeholders and analytics teams. Data Governance Stewardship role commitments are expected.

The Business Intelligence Analyst (BIA) has basic proficiency in SQL and data visualization, with the ability to learn on the job. The BIA has experience in stakeholder requirements

gathering and presentation skills. The primary responsibilities for the BIA include building dashboards, reporting, and trusted analytics content that is consumed by other analysts or stakeholders

Responsibilities

Communication and relationships -
The BIA acts a key Business Intelligence & Analytics liaison between hospital leadership, physician leadership, other clinical leaders, ISD and other stakeholders. They support departmental and organizational priorities. They serve as a guide of the organization's business intelligence priorities to internal constituents through formal and informal communications. The BIA develops concise, insightful, and politically savvy communications. These are often in PowerPoint, but also in email and verbally via committee meetings, staff meetings, and working sessions.

Dashboard and scorecard development -
The BIA develops effective key performance indicators, management dashboards and balanced scorecards that provide enhanced insight and improve organizational decision-making.

Healthcare analytics
- The BIA provides healthcare analytics support (e.g., predictive analytics, statistical analysis, data and text mining, data validation, prescriptive analysis) to generate insights that can be transformed into action and include a broad set of tools, processes, technologies, and stakeholders for collecting, integrating, accessing, and analyzing information. There may be fulfillment expectations of reporting and analytics requests.

Project management
-The BIA provides effective project management to clearly defines projects, develop project plans, and develops analytics to inform teams and guide prioritization.

Other Information

The Crown Is Yours

As a Senior Finance Data Analyst, you’ll turn complex financial and player activity data into reliable insights that support Accounting, financial reporting, and audit readiness. You’ll partner across Finance, Accounting, Data Engineering, and Analytics to connect operational activity with accurate, reconcilable financial data. You’ll strengthen our control environment by building repeatable processes, improving reporting automation, and maintaining clear data lineage and documentation for critical financial datasets and reports.

What you’ll do as a Senior Data Analyst

Build and automate financial reports, reconciliations, and analyses using SQL in Snowflake and reporting tools such as Tableau and Sigma.
Reconcile player activity, transactional systems, and financial datasets, investigating discrepancies and driving issues through resolution.
Partner with Accounting and Finance during financial close to investigate variances, validate data, and deliver supporting analyses.
Support internal and external audits by preparing data extracts, reconciliations, documentation, and control evidence.
Collaborate with Data Engineering and Analytics to define Finance-critical metrics, transformations, and reporting logic that connect source activity to financial reporting.
Design and maintain data controls, reconciliation procedures, data lineage, and documentation that strengthen the accuracy and integrity of financial reporting.
Shape how financial and operational data flows into the Financial System of Record and downstream reporting as new offerings, features, jurisdictions, and markets launch.
Identify opportunities to automate Finance and Accounting processes and translate reporting requirements into scalable data solutions.

What you’ll bring

A Bachelor’s Degree in a related field and 4+ years of experience in data analytics, financial analytics, accounting analytics, or another similar field.
Advanced SQL expertise, and experience analyzing large, complex transactional datasets.
Experience supporting financial reporting, accounting reconciliations, financial close processes, audits, or financial controls.
An understanding of financial data flows and accounting concepts with the ability to investigate discrepancies and identify root causes.
Experience with reporting and analytics tools such as Tableau, Sigma, Power BI, or Alteryx.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a focus on automation, process improvement, and repeatable solutions.
Strong communication, organization, and attention to detail, with the ability to collaborate across technical, Accounting, and Finance stakeholders.

jobs.title: GTM Strategy Analyst
jobs.description:
🚀 ¿Por qué trabajar en Xepelin?

Xepelin está transformando las finanzas empresariales en Latinoamérica con una suite de productos que automatizan la gestión financiera y facilitan el acceso a liquidez. Con el objetivo de convertirse en el CFO digital de todo negocio, ha desarrollado tecnología financiera que impacta en todo el ecosistema empresarial. Gracias a la data obtenida por la interacción de +1M de empresas dentro de su network , se construye un sistema de inteligencia de negocios que da visibilidad de indicadores financieros y evaluaciones de riesgo de la red con la que se colabora, ayudando a que la toma de decisiones sea más rápida y segura.

Nuestros principios ¿Cómo operamos?

🎯 Ponemos a nuestros clientes en el centro

✨ Creemos e inspiramos

🧑‍💼 Actuamos como dueños

🏅 Lideramos con el ejemplo

🏆 Nos desafiamos para ganar

🧠 Tomamos riesgos con inteligencia

🤖 Usamos el poder de la tecnología

¿Qué estamos buscando?

En Xepelin estamos buscando personas creativas y visionarias que piensen fuera de la caja para sumarse a nuestro equipo. Si te apasiona resolver desafíos interesantes de alto impacto y quieres ser parte de un entorno dinámico que está transformando la industria financiera, ¡Esta oportunidad es para ti!

Si te motiva el desafío de construir soluciones innovadoras en un entorno de rápido cambio, queremos conocerte.

Únete a nosotros, ¡crezcamos juntos!

Misión del rol

Ser el cerebro analítico detrás de la estrategia de crecimiento
de Xepelin México: definir dónde, cómo y a qué costo adquirimos clientes y convertir ese análisis en decisiones que el negocio ejecuta. El problema central es de los buenos: ¿dónde está el siguiente peso de crecimiento rentable?
¿Más Outbound, mejor pricing, otro segmento, un canal nuevo? Es un problema de asignación de capital, y tú eres quien lo modela, lo recomienda y lo acompaña hasta el resultado.

Principales responsabilidades

Estrategia de crecimiento y asignación de recursos: definir, junto al liderazgo del negocio, la estrategia de adquisición de la compañía — qué canales (Outbound, Inbound, Brokers, Digital), qué segmentos (SMB/Mid/Corp) y qué economics justifican cada inversión
Owner analítico del funnel completo: NQL→SQL→Enrolamiento→Aprobación→Activación→Retención. Diagnosticar dónde se pierde valor, cuantificar el tamaño de cada oportunidad y mantener un Control Tower con CAC, payback, LTV y Gross Profit por canal, levantando alertas cuando algo se desvía de la tesis
Resolución de problemas estratégicos (tu día a día estilo consultoría): estructurar problemas ambiguos en análisis accionables — descomponer una caída de ventas en tasa × ticket × volumen, diagnosticar un funnel SDR, dimensionar un canal nuevo con un business case
Pricing & elegibilidad (con Riesgo): modelar bandas de precio/score-cut y diseñar/leer experimentos A/B que equilibren aprobación y margen
Research de cliente: entrevistas, jobs-to-be-done e insights de mercado que se traducen en ofertas, mensajes y apuestas de segmento
De la recomendación a la ejecución: bajar la estrategia a instrumentos operables — playbooks de Outbound, lead scoring, territories, listas activables (AI/enrichment), briefs de Digital — y coordinar handoffs con SDR/AE, Marketing y Growth
Cadencia operativa: preparar y facilitar WBR/MBR. No reportas métricas: cuentas la historia del negocio, propones la decisión y das seguimiento a los compromisos
Experimentación y gobierno de datos: priorizar hipótesis, diseñar tests, instrumentar tracking, productizar ganadores (playbook + métricas); definir eventos, taxonomías y QA de tracking con Analytics/Eng

¿Qué necesitas para brillar?

Pensamiento estructurado: descompones problemas ambiguos en árboles de hipótesis, priorizas el análisis que mueve la decisión y comunicas con claridad ejecutiva (escrita y verbal)
Estratega operador(a): la recomendación no te basta; bajas la idea a dashboard, playbook y piloto en días, no semanas
Data chops: SQL intermedio-avanzado, manejo de BigQuery/Looker o equivalentes; familiaridad con causalidad/experimentos y métricas de funnel
AI driven: experto en Claude/Chat GPT/Gemini/otros, con casos de uso claros y con impacto
Track record de impacto en KPIs: has movido números concretos — enrolamientos, aprobación, activación, churn — y puedes contar el cómo, no solo el cuánto
Obsesión por el cliente: research continuo, entrevistas, jobs-to-be-done, y capacidad de transformar insights en ofertas y mensajes accionables
Influencia cross-functional: te mueves con Revenue, Growth, Riesgo, Producto y Finanzas con la misma comodidad, sin autoridad formal
Owner mindset: foco en impacto económico (CAC, payback, margen, LTV), no en entregables

Requisitos

2+ años en consultoría estratégica o roles GTM/Strategy/Growth/RevOps analíticos, ideal con foco en adquisición B2B (fintech, SaaS, pagos o lending es plus)
Experiencia probada gestionando funnel completo y mejorando KPIs (enrolamientos, aprobación, activación, churn)
SQL (intermedio a avanzado) y Excel/Sheets avanzado
La posición es para CDMX. Si actualmente estás en Chile pero tienes disponibilidad para mudarte a Ciudad de México, esta oportunidad puede ser para ti.

Nuestros Beneficios:

🌴 Xepelin Balance

Vacaciones:
15 días hábiles. Por cada año que cumplas en Xepelin, te damos un día extra de vacaciones.

Balance days:
10 días libres adicionales al año, para disfrutar como quieras.

Beneficios Flexibles:
Puntos flexibles en tu moneda local al mes para gastar en lo que quieras.

🚀 Xepelin Performance & Career

Plataformas de capacitación:
Convenios con las mejores plataformas, como Udemy y Google Cloud Skill Boost.

Kit de Bienvenida:
todo lo que necesitas para comenzar tu viaje en Xepelin 😊

contamos con convenios de salud con proveedores de calidad o reembolsos según el país donde te encuentres.

Post Natal:
te damos una semana extra de licencia post natal. ¡Nos interesa que estés con tu familia y seres queridos!

Matrimonio plus:
Lleva tus planes al siguiente nivel, con una gift card y extendiendo tu permiso legal por matrimonio con dos días de regalo por Xepelin.

Role Overview

We are seeking a senior Technical Project Manager (Tech PM) with deep domain expertise in Apple Enterprise Infrastructure to lead the modernization and deployment of our enterprise macOS endpoint management platform. Managing a fleet of ~15,000 users and ~40,000 multi-platform endpoints (Windows, Cloud PC, iOS, Android, and Ubuntu), this role primarily focuses on driving the strategic project delivery, roadmap execution, and operational alignment for modernizing macOS architecture using Microsoft Intune at scale.
The Tech PM will bridge the gap between engineering teams, cybersecurity leads, executive leadership, and enterprise stakeholders. You will manage technical delivery schedules, risk mitigations, cross-functional dependencies, and deployment roadmaps across corporate, R&D lab, and manufacturing environments.

Key Responsibilities

Program & Technical Project Delivery:
Lead end-to-end project execution for modernizing enterprise macOS and iOS management using Microsoft Intune and Apple Business Manager (ABM/DEP), ensuring on-time delivery across ~40,000 endpoints.
Architecture & Migration Governance:
Manage project roadmaps, milestones, and technical dependencies for migrating macOS devices from legacy frameworks (e.g., Jamf Pro) to Intune, including enterprise application packaging, patching, and OS upgrades.
Security & Compliance Alignment:
Partner with Information Security teams to schedule, track, and validate the rollout of macOS security baselines—including FileVault encryption key escrow, Defender for Endpoint, Platform SSO (PSSO), and Entra ID Conditional Access rules.
Stakeholder & Change Management:

Cross-Platform Delivery Alignment:
Coordinate delivery schedules across multi-platform teams to maintain alignment between macOS infrastructure, Windows/Cloud PC rollouts, mobile device management (iOS/Android), and secondary Ubuntu environments.
Vendor & Lifecycle Management:
Oversee technical relationships with Apple, Microsoft, and third-party software vendors. Track hardware procurement timelines, device lifecycle refresh programs, and enterprise licensing requirements.
Operational Readiness & Telemetry:
Define project success metrics, KPI dashboards, and telemetry reports for leadership. Oversee operational handoffs, technical runbook documentation, and Tier 1–3 support training programs.

Qualifications

Experience:
7+ years in IT Technical Project Management focused on Enterprise End User Computing (EUC) and Infrastructure, with explicit experience leading enterprise macOS or modern device management projects at scale (10,000+ endpoints).
Technical Domain Knowledge:
Solid technical understanding of Apple Business Manager (ABM), Microsoft Intune (or Jamf Pro migration projects), macOS Platform SSO, FileVault, and Entra ID integration.
Project Methodology:
Proven track record managing complex IT infrastructure initiatives using Agile, Scrum, or hybrid PM methodologies. Proficiency with Jira, Confluence, Microsoft Project, or Azure DevOps for backlog and sprint tracking.
Security & Compliance Awareness:
Experience coordinating rollouts involving endpoint security agents (Microsoft Defender, CrowdStrike, Jamf Protect) and identity workflows (MFA, Conditional Access, SSO extensions).
Leadership & Communication:
Exceptional stakeholder management skills, with the proven ability to articulate complex technical risks, timelines, and architectural decisions to executive leadership and technical teams alike.

jobs.description:
About Rivian

Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.

As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.

Role Summary

The well-qualified candidate will be responsible for the development and delivery execution of electrical

power conversion (EPC) Electrical Hardware for charging and vehicle products. This role requires a high

level of initiative, independent judgement, and indirect leadership capability.

Responsibilities

You will be responsible for driving the design, development, release, and validation for different Rivian

Electric Power Conversion Electrical Hardware projects. In this role you will collaborate with cross

functional teams to align on overall program deliverables and report on status and risks to ensure

visibility across teams.

Strategic Project Leadership: Drive the end-to-end design, development, release, and validation

of Rivian Electric Power Conversion Electrical Hardware projects, demonstrating strong

independent judgment and indirect leadership.

Cross-Functional Collaboration: Serve as the primary liaison between the EPC electrical

hardware team and cross-functional partners to align on overall program deliverables, providing

clear status updates and proactively identifying and mitigating risks.

Detailed Timeline Management: Collaborate with the EPC electrical hardware team to establish

comprehensive high-level timelines and milestones, meticulously tracking critical release dates,

Material Requirement Dates (MRDs), validation plans, and industrialization support.

In-House Development Oversight: Spearhead the development of in-house PCBA designs and

assemblies, ensuring adherence to quality and performance standards.

Supply Chain and BOM Management: Take ownership of BOM release and component sourcing

in collaboration with the supply chain team. Proactively track long-lead parts and tool order

needs, coordinating closely with the supply chain team on due dates and status throughout the

development lifecycle.

Production Lifecycle Management: Lead engineering releases, manage prototype builds, and

oversee production start-up, ensuring prompt resolution of any build issues. Manage the ok2x

product development process.

Contract Manufacturing Coordination: Facilitate seamless coordination with Contract

Manufacturing Suppliers and the supply chain to guarantee timely delivery of components and

assemblies.

Validation Activity Oversight: Coordinate, track, and report on Design Validation (DV) and

Process Validation (PV) activities to ensure product robustness and manufacturing readiness.

Effective Communication: Maintain prompt, clear, and actionable communication with the

Product Delivery team to facilitate successful execution and achieve program objectives.

Budget Management: Plan and meticulously track budgets for EPC electrical hardware, testing,

and validation activities.

Issue Resolution & Continuous Improvement: Implement robust issue tracking and corrective

action processes, utilizing tools such as JIRA, to drive continuous improvement.

Stakeholder Interfacing: Interface effectively with diverse cross-functional teams, including

Design Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, and Supply Chain, providing cohesive leadership

and bridging gaps as needed.

Qualifications

Requirements:

Familiarity with charging products, electric power conversion, electrical hardware design.
Management of ECUs, including PCBAs for multiple projects.
Understanding of the PCBA design and manufacturing processes.
Experience coordinating with contract manufacturers.
Bachelor’s degree in an engineering/technology field or equivalent work experience.
8+ years of automotive program management experience.

Preferred

Electrical Engineering background.

Required Skillsets

Understanding of automotive engineering release processes.
Proficiency in program management processes and vehicle development timeline tools (e.g.,

Smartsheet, JIRA, Confluence, Vizzlo).

Experience in creating and implementing new program management processes.
Ability to collaborate and communicate effectively with cross-functional teams.
Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.

Pay Disclosure

The salary range for this role is $154,000 - $192,500 for Carson, CA-based applicants. This is the lowest-to-highest salary we, in good faith, believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs. The successful candidate may be eligible for an annual performance bonus and equity awards.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information or characteristics, physical or mental disability, marital/domestic partner status, age, military/veteran status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you have a disability or limitation, such as those covered by the Americans with Disabilities Act, that requires accommodations to assist you in the search and application process, please email us at candidateaccommodations@rivian.com.

Candidate Data Privacy and Technology

Rivian may collect, use and disclose your personal information or personal data (within the meaning of the applicable data protection laws) when you apply for employment and/or participate in our recruitment processes (“Candidate Personal Data”). This data includes contact, demographic, communications, educational, professional, employment, social media/website, network/device, recruiting system usage/interaction, security and preference information. Rivian may use your Candidate Personal Data for the purposes of (i) tracking interactions with our recruiting system; (ii) carrying out, analyzing and improving our application and recruitment process, including assessing you and your application and conducting employment, background and reference checks; (iii) establishing an employment relationship or entering into an employment contract with you; (iv) complying with our legal, regulatory and corporate governance obligations; (v) recordkeeping; (vi) ensuring network and information security and preventing fraud; and (vii) as otherwise required or permitted by applicable law.

Rivian may share your Candidate Personal Data with (i) internal personnel who have a need to know such information in order to perform their duties, including individuals on our People Team, Finance, Legal, and the team(s) with the position(s) for which you are applying; (ii) Rivian affiliates; and (iii) Rivian’s service providers, including providers of background checks, staffing services, and cloud services.

jobs.title: Research Program Manager, Governance
jobs.description:
About The Team

OpenAI’s Governance team helps shape how the company responsibly develops and deploys increasingly capable AI. We bring together technical evidence, policy, and operational perspectives to help the company address emerging risks, resolve difficult questions, and make well-supported decisions.

Our work includes shaping and improving governance practices, supporting effective oversight, developing clear assessments and recommendations, and ensuring that decisions lead to action. We work closely with research, safety, security, legal, and product teams to identify gaps, reconcile different views, and improve our approach as capabilities and circumstances change.

About The Role

We are looking for a curious, high-agency Research Program Manager who can reason from first principles, make sense of incomplete or conflicting information, and move difficult work forward. You will help shape the substance of governance reviews, connect ideas and evidence across teams, and develop recommendations that are both well-founded and practical.

The work requires someone who can use established approaches where they fit, recognize when circumstances call for a different approach, and update their thinking as new evidence emerges. You should bring sound judgment, a willingness to experiment and learn, and the program-management discipline to turn good analysis into action.

Depending on your experience and the team’s needs, your work may focus on safety advisory and board-level oversight, deployment governance, or standards and strategic partner commitments.

In This Role, You Will

Bring together technical, policy, and operational inputs to develop coherent assessments, recommendations, and decision materials for governance bodies and senior leaders.
Work through emerging or ambiguous questions, test assumptions, identify gaps or conflicting evidence, and help determine what additional analysis or decisions are needed.
Engage critically with research, evaluations, safeguards, and risk assessments, working with the relevant experts to understand what the evidence supports and where uncertainty remains.
Partner with governance-body chairs, technical leaders, and other stakeholders to shape substantive reviews, frame the questions that matter, and communicate conclusions clearly.
Translate feedback, recommendations, and decisions into concrete work with accountable owners, milestones, dependencies, and clear criteria for completion.

jobs.title: Staff Program Manager, Organizational Change Management
jobs.description:
Overview

Intuit's CTREC organization (Cybersecurity, Trust & Safety, Risk, Enterprise Systems and Compliance) protects the company and powers the technology experiences of our global workforce. We're looking for a Senior Change Manager to own organizational change management (OCM) delivery and adoption strategy for CTREC's most critical programs — the changes that touch every Intuit employee, from security protocols to enterprise systems to employee-experience technology.

This is a hands-on leadership role, not an advisory one. You will craft the change strategy for each program and personally execute every piece of it — communications across channels, enablement content, stakeholder engagement, and adoption measurement. There is no separate design or communications team behind you, and no runway to learn the discipline on the job. Skilled, self-directed OCM leadership is essential to adoption success from day one.

You'll operate as part of the Change COE — the team that designs the human layer around technology change so employees don't just get access to something new; they understand it, want it, and can use it well. The COE matches its response to the size and risk of each change: it Drives the highest-impact changes end to end, Supports moderate ones by contributing strategy while the owning team executes, and Consults as the fast expert check on lower-risk changes. You'll flex across all three modes and partner with the OCM lead to define the engagement model and tiered level of support for each initiative.

Responsibilities

Own end-to-end OCM delivery and adoption strategy for critical CTREC programs — from impact assessment through launch, adoption, and reinforcement.
Build change strategy from scratch and execute it end to end yourself: audience and impact analysis, adoption plans, success metrics, and risk mitigation — with no reliance on separate design or communications resources.
Develop and deliver communications for multiple channels (email, Slack, intranet, in-tool messaging, executive briefings), right-sized to audience and moment.
Create enablement content — guides, FAQs, training assets, self-service resources — that helps a distributed global workforce understand, embrace, and adopt change.
Drive stakeholder engagement across all levels, from frontline employees to senior leadership, building the coalitions each change needs to land.
Partner closely with Development, the Product lead, and the Technical Program Manager as an embedded member of the program team, and align strategy with the OCM lead.
Flex across the Change COE's engagement tiers — Drive, Support, or Consult — matching depth of involvement to the size and risk of each change, and partner with the OCM lead to define engagement models and tiered levels of support across the portfolio.
Invent creative, low-friction adoption solutions — resourceful ways to reach and activate distributed audiences and build trust in automation that acts on a user's behalf.
Develop and implement change management tools and processes that accelerate change activities, ensure a consistent change experience, and standardize communication approaches across programs.
Monitor employee feedback channels to address questions and gauge sentiment on Security change initiatives, feeding insights back into program decisions.
Measure adoption, gather feedback, and iterate — closing the loop between user sentiment and program decisions.

Qualifications

7+ years of change management experience supporting large, multi-site enterprise implementations of HR, IT service, Security, or employee-experience technology.
Proven ability to own change strategy from scratch and execute it end to end personally — you are the strategist, writer, designer, and facilitator in one.
A track record of creative, low-friction adoption solutions that reached and activated distributed audiences — including building user trust in automation acting on their behalf.
AI platform fluency — you use AI tools and platforms fluently in your own work (research, content development, analysis) and can guide others through AI-driven change.
Excellent writing and content-design skills across formats and channels, with the judgment to right-size comms to the change.
Strong stakeholder management — comfortable partnering with engineering, product, and program leaders and influencing without authority.
Self-direction and speed: you scope ambiguity into a plan, prioritize independently, and deliver without needing the role explained to you.
Strong proficiency applying ADKAR or an equivalent structured change methodology within condensed go-live timelines and high stakeholder expectations.
Proven ability to manage concurrent workloads under a fixed deadline, sequencing communications across phased waves to prevent audience fatigue and message conflicts.
Strong executive communication skills — comfortable drafting on behalf of senior HR and technology leadership for enterprise-wide distribution.
Domain experience across collaboration SaaS applications, HR, and Security, with a working understanding of data security and compliance concepts.
Skilled in impact analysis, stakeholder mapping, and developing communication and care/readiness plans.
Technology company experience implementing change efforts that impact technologist/development organizations as well as business functions.
Project management experience leading cross-functional teams to achieve business goals.

Who You Are

Customer obsessed — inspired by the customer problem, partnering with process owners to drive change, education, and outreach.
A strong process and systems thinker, sees how changes, channels, and audiences interact across a portfolio, and builds repeatable tools, standards, and mechanisms rather than one-off fixes.
Demonstrates extreme ownership, delivers excellence at scale, and operates without boundaries.
Influences and drives decisions by crafting a clear point of view — options, data-backed recommendations, and rationale — and builds a compelling, data-backed case for change.
Proactively identifies obstacles, develops recommendations for resolution, and escalates to leaders quickly.
Quickly establishes credibility and trust across teams; leads with inquiry and incorporates diverse perspectives to deliver high-impact outcomes.
Resilient and solution-oriented in a high-change, often ambiguous environment, with a data-led and data-driven approach focused on long-term opportunity.
Proactive, action-oriented self-starter with high judgment, innovation, and strategic thinking; strong organizational and time-management skills.
Works independently and collaborates effectively across cross-functional teams and with employees at all levels, using inquiry and advocacy to work through barriers.

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

We’re a team of friends bound together by a mission to preserve our planet for future generations through innovative energy solutions and modern infrastructure. Intersect develops, constructs, and operates the most ambitious power and data center infrastructure in the country by co-locating industrial demand with dedicated gas and renewable power generation.

Intersect was acquired by Google in March 2026 and operates as an independent subsidiary. We are developing and constructing multiple gigawatts of energy and data center projects in the U.S., enabling more data center and generation capacity to come online faster. We’re on an aggressive growth trajectory and looking for people hungry to tackle the largest energy challenges on the planet.

Location & Team Gatherings

Intersect has been a fully flexible workplace since its founding in 2016.  We’ve been very intentional about the way we do things. We are not work-from-home, hybrid, or in-office - we are any and all of those options! Deepening social connections and offering shared experiences is a cornerstone of the way we work. We connect as a team at our Team Week experiences four times a year and at our recently established Hub locations - SF Bay Area, NYC Metro Area, NY; Denver, CO; Austin, TX; Calgary, AB; and Toronto, ON.

We are currently looking for candidates located within 60 miles of any of the listed hubs to foster more in-person connections while maintaining our flexible remote culture.

About This Role

As part of Intersect’s project delivery organization, you’ll lead the execution of critical power generation and energy infrastructure projects that support the convergence of electrification, digitalization, and decarbonization. Acting as the owner’s representative throughout the project lifecycle, you’ll guide complex projects from development through commissioning and commercial operation while partnering closely with engineering, construction, commercial, operations, and executive leadership teams.

You’ll oversee the successful delivery of natural gas-fired power generation facilities and related infrastructure, including reciprocating engine plants, gas turbine facilities, HV switchyards, substations, battery energy storage systems (BESS), generation assets, and large-scale data center power infrastructure. Success requires strong technical judgment, disciplined project execution, and the ability to align diverse stakeholders around safety, quality, schedule, budget, and long-term value creation.

This role is planned to start as soon as practical based on project requirements. A training and onboarding period of approximately two weeks is anticipated, with the expectation that the successful candidate will contribute immediately, become actively engaged during the first week, and achieve full organizational integration within the first two months.

Team Overview

This team plays a critical role in advancing Intersect’s mission to accelerate the clean energy transition through the development and execution of large-scale energy infrastructure projects. By bringing together expertise across development, engineering, construction, commercial operations, and asset management, the team delivers the integrated infrastructure required to support a more reliable, scalable, and sustainable energy future.

Joining this team provides the opportunity to work on highly visible projects with significant industry impact while collaborating alongside experienced professionals who are shaping the next generation of energy infrastructure. The team values accountability, innovation, continuous learning, and cross-functional partnership, creating an environment where individuals can grow professionally while contributing to meaningful outcomes.

What You’ll Do

Lead Complex Project Execution

Develop and execute comprehensive project plans, including scope definition, execution strategy, resource planning, governance structures, and delivery objectives.

Lead natural gas-fired power generation projects from development through commissioning and commercial operation.

Drive project performance against key objectives related to safety, quality, schedule, budget, and operational readiness.

Facilitate project closeout activities, lessons learned, commissioning support, and successful turnover to operations teams.

Manage EPC and External Partner Performance

Serve as the primary owner’s representative and point of contact for EPC contractors, consultants, utilities, equipment vendors, and key stakeholders.

Oversee contractor performance, contract compliance, commercial negotiations, change management activities, and claims resolution.

Review and approve construction strategies, procurement plans, and execution methodologies.

Build productive relationships across complex stakeholder groups to support successful project outcomes.

Drive Project Controls and Risk Management

Develop and maintain project schedules, budgets, forecasts, risk registers, and reporting frameworks.

Implement project controls processes that improve visibility into cost, schedule, and execution performance.

Lead risk identification, mitigation planning, and issue resolution activities throughout the project lifecycle.

Provide clear, actionable project updates to senior leadership and executive stakeholders.

Deliver Technical Excellence

Partner with engineering teams to review and approve technical designs, engineering deliverables, vendor submittals, and construction approaches.

Support the integration of reciprocating engine facilities, gas turbine plants, HV substations and switchyards, utility interconnections, BESS assets, generation resources, and data center infrastructure.

Ensure technical solutions align with project objectives, operational requirements, and long-term asset performance expectations.

Drive quality assurance and quality control processes across engineering, procurement, construction, and commissioning activities.

Champion Safety and Regulatory Compliance

Foster a culture of safety excellence across all project activities and stakeholder groups.

Conduct site inspections, audits, and field reviews to verify adherence to safety requirements, project specifications, and quality standards.

Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, environmental obligations, permitting requirements, and applicable energy-sector standards.

Support safe and compliant project execution while maintaining a focus on continuous improvement and operational excellence.

Build Alignment Across Teams

Partner with engineering, construction, commercial, operations, and executive leadership teams to drive decision-making and project success.

Facilitate collaboration across internal and external stakeholders to resolve challenges and maintain project momentum.

Promote accountability, transparency, and strong communication throughout project execution.

Help cultivate a high-performing environment centered on technical excellence, ownership, and long-term value creation.

What You’ll Bring

Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Architectural Engineering, Construction Management, or a related engineering or design discipline.

10+ years of progressive experience in project execution, construction management, engineering management, or project leadership within power generation, energy infrastructure, oil & gas, utility, or heavy industrial sectors.

Demonstrated experience executing projects from either the Owner’s side or Contractor/EPC side through development, engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operational handover.

Direct experience supporting the construction and execution of natural gas-fired power generation projects.

Knowledge of quality assurance, commissioning, startup activities, and safety management systems.

Exceptional communication, stakeholder management, negotiation, and leadership skills.

A hands-on leadership style that balances strategic oversight with detailed execution and accountability.

Resilience, sound judgment, and composure when navigating competing priorities and complex stakeholder environments.

A commitment to collaboration, continuous learning, inclusion, and long-term value creation aligned with Intersect’s values of Equity, Humility, Authenticity, Long-run Value, and People Come First.

$188,500 - $205,400 (total compensation includes base salary + bonus in USD)

Equity:
Beyond your salary, you’ll receive an Equity Grant, giving you a meaningful stake in our parent company.

Up to 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, plus 6 additional weeks for birth parents; access to family planning and family care support through Carrot and Maven

Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is seeking a Project Manager, Power & Energy
for our Power & Energy Program Management Office in Tulsa, OK
. The following locations will also be considered: Oklahoma City, OK; Dallas, TX; Austin, TX; Houston, TX; Corpus Christi, TX; Bentonville, AR; and Shreveport, LA.
The successful candidate may work remotely within the United States and must have the ability to travel to a WSP and/or Client office for periodic face-to-face meetings.

Your Impact

Provides technical project supervision, and guidance with managing the administrative, commercial, and technical components of assigned project(s) in accordance with WSP’s core values and the level of project services agreed upon in the contract by WSP and the client(s). Tasks include responsibility for the overall performance of the assigned project(s) that are of moderate size/complexity and/or local/regional in scope, and includes oversight for financial, technical, client satisfaction, quality, safety, and schedule. Ensures that responsibilities throughout the project lifecycle (proposal phase, project startup and planning, project execution, reporting, and project closeout) are adhered to, delivered, and audited with a level of quality that meets or exceeds acceptable corporate standards for safety, execution, profitability, and operational purpose.

Oversee and monitor cross-functional teams of technical professionals to execute project work on mid-level and/or multiple concurrent projects, including budgets, tracking hours and expenses, task completion, cost and quantities of materials/equipment/labor, deliverables, compliance documentation, and managing the contractual obligations to deliver the project(s) as defined in the contract.
Play a contributing role in the development of project proposals, cost estimates, scope, schedules, and resource plans.
Develop the work breakdown structure (WBS) tasks and estimated costs.
Establish the level of technical review required for the project, selecting appropriately qualified staff to perform the required reviews, and adherence to the QA/QC plan, as applicable.
Contribute to performing margin analyses, establishing margin goals and risk contingencies.
Coordinate and assist with the technical aspects of contract negotiation, presentation, and meetings.
Develop and update the Project Initiation/Setup Documentation including: Risk (REF/RMP), Project Management Plan (PMP), Project Quality Plan (QP), Project Safety (PSP), and Communications Plan as necessary.
Participate in project kick-off meetings with key stakeholders.
Work collaboratively with Project Accounting to monitor and track project metrics, estimated time-to-completion, cash management, and budgeted margin for a project or an assigned portfolio of projects.
Oversee management of budgeting, forecasting, scheduling, cost and change management and control. Support integrated project controls activities, including schedule and cost performance tracking, forecast updates, variance analysis, change tracking, progress measurement, and preparation of performance dashboards and executive-level reporting.
Coordinate with area/technical managers to address project resource and subcontracting requirements in a timely manner. Immediately communicate and escalate any project site Health & Safety or significant client issues to senior PM staff and leadership.
Participate in problem project reviews, providing input about root cause issues and potential solutions to leadership and other stakeholders.
Provide regular project reporting and updates to clients, technical area, and business unit managers, identifying any emergent issues with scope, risk, and/or budget.
Coordinate closely with client representatives, internal delivery teams, functional leads, subcontractors, and external stakeholders to align priorities, clarify responsibilities, resolve issues, and support consistent execution across assigned work.
Monitor accounts receivable (AR) and unbilled revenue, working to address issues as needed. Work with the Procurement Department to closeout procurements and/or supplier agreements as appropriate.
Complete formal project closeout activities, along with conducting and documenting a lessons-learned meeting with key project staff.
Remain current in the latest Project Management techniques and practices (PMAP).
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, science, or a related major, or equivalent experience in a technical or engineering firm.
Essential project management certification required (e.g., PMP, CAP-M).
7 to 10 years of relevant post education experience in a project management role within our industry.
Sound understanding of project delivery process within the A/E/C industry and well-defined background and experience in project management.
Well-developed analytical and organizational skills, with business acumen to bridge the business and project management.
Competent critical thinking and problem-solving skills to make assessments and calculations involving the application of project management principles, with a sound understanding of intent, impact, and optimal outcomes.
Highly effective interpersonal and communication skills when interacting with others, expressing ideas effectively and professionally.
Demonstrated high-level of self-leadership with attention to detail, multi-tasking, and adjusting readily to the changing prioritization of responsibilities in a dynamic work environment. Works independently with minimal oversight and provides guidance and leadership to junior team or project members, with strict adherence to QA/QC.
Competent with technical writing, office automation, relevant software, MS Office suite products (e.g., Word, Excel, Visio, Project, SharePoint), technology, spreadsheets, and PM tools.
Demonstrated effectiveness at coordinating resources and assertively directing consultants, suppliers, subcontractors, and others to complete tasks competently and efficiently.
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.
Ability to work schedules conducive to project-specific requirements that may extend beyond the typical workweek.
Occasional travel may be required depending on project-specific requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s Degree in Engineering

WSP Benefits

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

About WSP

ABOUT US

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. WSP USA designs lasting solutions in the buildings, transportation, energy, water and environment markets. new_jobs.title: Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is seeking an experienced Project Manager to provide oversight in support of the Puerto Rico Public Housing Administration’s (PRPHA) Program Management Services for Permeant Works Program (FEMA). The Project Manager is responsible for the day-to-day management, coordination, monitoring, and execution of assigned projects. This role ensures that project activities, deliverables, schedules, budgets, and compliance requirements are effectively managed throughout planning, procurement, construction, and closeout phases.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Position Summary

The Project Manager will serve as the primary operational lead for assigned projects and will work closely with PRPHA, oversight teams, consultants, contractors, and internal project staff.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions:

Manage and coordinate assigned projects through planning, scope validation, bid package development, procurement support, construction monitoring, and project closeout.
Lead and coordinate the validation of project scopes of work and quantities.
Coordinate the preparation, review, completeness verification, and delivery of bid packages to the Management Agent.
Monitor project schedules, budgets, risks, issues, dependencies, and critical decision points.
Coordinate activities among engineers, estimators, procurement and compliance personnel, financial management specialists, administrative staff, and other project resources.
Identify and document discrepancies, omissions, inconsistencies, or changes that may impact project scope, quantities, budget, schedule, procurement activities, or compliance requirements.
Coordinate with PRPHA, oversight teams, Management Agents, designers, consultants, contractors, and stakeholders to support successful project delivery.
Maintain current project information, including milestones, deliverables, risks, project status, and action items.
Prepare and manage project status reports, dashboards, meeting agendas, meeting minutes, action logs, and other project management documentation.
Support the Program Director with reporting, planning, risk management, and program-level decision-making.
Monitor project activities during construction from a project management and controls perspective without duplicating construction inspection responsibilities.
Support project closeout activities and ensure the collection and completeness of required project documentation.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree from an accredited university in either Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Project Management, Business Administration, or a related field
Minimum three (3) years of professional experience in Project management services, Project coordination activities, or Procurement and bid process support services
Experience working with municipal governments, public agencies, housing programs, or community development initiatives.
Fluency in English and Spanish, including the ability to prepare professional documents and presentations in both languages.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience managing public infrastructure, housing, rehabilitation, or capital improvement projects.
Experience supporting disaster recovery initiatives.
Familiarity with FEMA-funded projects and Public Assistance programs.
Experience working with HUD-funded projects and federal grant compliance requirements.
Strong stakeholder coordination, reporting, and project controls experience.
Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Physical Requirements

All candidates must be in Puerto Rico to be considered for the position.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

This is an on-site position with intermittent travel to job sites or client meetings on the island.

Compensation

The salary range for this position is $90,000 – $95,000 (depending on experience). The base salary range represents the low and high end of the compensation scale for this role. Actual salaries will be determined based on location, experience, responsibilities, and qualifications.

Additional Information

Employment Type: Full-time (contingent upon award)
Work Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8AM–5PM (no expected overtime)
Travel Requirements: 10%–20% (for supervision/coordination activities)
Work Location: San Juan, Puerto Rico

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

About Tetra Tech

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. With 30,000 employees working together, Tetra Tech provides clear solutions to complex problems by Leading with Science® to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Tetra Tech is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, marital or familial status, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law. Tetra Tech is a VEVRAA federal contractor, and we request priority referral of veterans.

We invite applications from all interested parties.

Explore our open positions at https://www.tetratech.com/careers. Follow us on social media to learn more about our people, culture, and opportunities:

LinkedIn: @TetraTechCareers

X (Twitter): @TetraTechJobs

We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

Please no phone calls or agencies.

new_jobs.description:
Description

Enterprise Knowledge (EK)
is hiring a full-time Project Manager
to join our growing Enterprise Delivery team. This individual will manage business strategy and technical delivery projects for a range of commercial and federal clients. As with all of our positions, we are seeking independent thinkers with creative problem-solving skills.

As a Project Manager Consultant
, you will take ownership of projects leading complex engagements that meet both client expectations and business objectives. You'll drive project planning and road mapping, keeping schedules, budgets, and stakeholder communications on track while ensuring the team stays focused on overarching goals rather than just individual deliverables. You'll serve as a key voice in client-facing meetings, articulating business value, navigating change requests strategically, and representing EK's capabilities to build trust and expand engagement opportunities. This role calls for someone who thrives on structure and follow-through—someone who can facilitate high-stakes conversations, document and drive decisions to closure, and keep projects organized and moving even amid ambiguity.

As an EKer, you will join a fast-growing company that is committed to equity and inclusion, have the opportunity to work in a collaborative workplace, take advantage of our unique benefits
, and help build our innovative culture. To read more about the impactful work we are doing and to see the latest thought leadership from EK, follow us on LinkedIn
.

Responsibilities

Develop, maintain, and monitor project plans, project schedules, and work hours
Lead and deliver projects and products that exceed client expectations within the project budget
Plan, execute, manage, and deliver large projects from strategy and design to implementation.
Manage and facilitate stakeholder meetings and project deadlines
Create a project roadmap for fulfilling each project goal and objective
Manage delivery to project goals and objectives rather than solely focused on deliverables
Navigate Change Request processes as required in order to maximize business and strategic outcomes
Facilitate meetings and present during them to communicate project status, articulate business value, and market EK’s services
Document and follow up on important actions and decisions from meetings
Proactively ensure important tasks and decisions are taking place on schedule
Support requirements gathering facilitation by preparing the necessary presentation materials for meetings
Undertake project tasks and assist with project strategies through implementation
Ensure documentation is maintained and organized appropriately for each project

Requirements

As a federal contractor, Enterprise Knowledge will not sponsor a new applicant for employment authorization or offer any immigration related support for this position (i.e., H1B, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, F-1 CPT, J-1, TN, E-2, E-3, L-1, and O-1, or any EADs or other forms of work authorization that require immigration support from an employer.

This hybrid role requires that you live within a comfortable, commutable distance of our Arlington, VA office and be willing to be on-site 2 days a week.

Required Skills And Experience

Bachelor’s Degree in business, IT, or a related field of study
4-8 years of experience managing business strategy and technical projects that require client/ stakeholder interaction
Experience working in the different stages of the SDLC.
Manage multiple projects simultaneously and prioritize work to appropriately
Comfort with navigating ambiguity and rapidly evolving client needs.
Ability to quickly learn new technical concepts with minimal guidance
Manage and mentor team members
Experience working with Agile teams and familiar with Agile methodologies (Scrum, Kanban)
Experience managing project financials for commercial and/or federal projects

Preferred Skills And Qualifications

PMP certification
Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO)
Certified Scrum Master (CSM)
Familiarity with project management tools (ie, Trello, JIRA, Monday, etc.)

Salary Information

EK considers a broad range of factors in considering employee salary, including a candidate’s skills, experience, education, certifications, past successes, and qualifications. The salary range for this role is $125,000 to $150,000, with most candidates likely to fall in the lower half. This range does not guarantee a specific salary and may be adjusted based on the needs of the company and the candidate’s qualifications.
